evidence.claim: Before the invasion, Scholz warned Russia of serious political, economic, and strategic consequences if it escalated against Ukraine, while also saying Germany and its allies were ready for dialogue and wanted peace.
evidence.title: Germany's Scholz warns Russia over Ukraine, but says 'we want peace'
evidence.excerpt: Before the invasion, Scholz warned Russia of serious political, economic, and strategic consequences if it escalated against Ukraine, while also saying Germany and its allies were ready for dialogue and wanted peace.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting via a reputable outlet; strong contemporaneous coverage of Scholz's prewar posture.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Scholz conduct and messaging; attributable to the ruler, not inherited policy.
contrary_evidence: Warnings are not the same as concrete risk-reduction measures.
The source is a mediated Reuters report, not a transcript.

evidence.claim: Scholz tied Germany's response to the Ukraine invasion to a modern replacement for the Tornado jets for nuclear sharing, while also calling for stronger resilience against cyberattacks, disinformation, and attacks on critical infrastructure.
evidence.title: Policy statement by Olaf Scholz, Chancellor of the Federal Republic of Germany, 27 February 2022 in Berlin
evidence.excerpt: Scholz tied Germany's response to the Ukraine invasion to a modern replacement for the Tornado jets for nuclear sharing, while also calling for stronger resilience against cyberattacks, disinformation, and attacks on critical infrastructure.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government speech; excellent for dated policy commitments and ruler attribution.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in-period and central to 2022 security policy.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Scholz personally announced the policy direction, though implementation depended on cabinet and allies.
contrary_evidence: Speech gives intent and framing, not implementation or outcomes.
Official rhetoric may emphasize resolve over delay or dissent.

evidence.claim: Germany moved to buy 35 F-35 fighters to replace its ageing Tornado aircraft in the nuclear-sharing role, marking a concrete follow-through on the February shift.
evidence.title: Berlin wants to buy 35 Lockheed F-35 fighter jets, def min tells parliament
evidence.excerpt: Germany moved to buy 35 F-35 fighters to replace its ageing Tornado aircraft in the nuclear-sharing role, marking a concrete follow-through on the February shift.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report with a clear dated procurement decision; strong corroboration of the chancellor's policy line.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and tightly tied to the nuclear-sharing posture.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Scholz's government and security policy direction, even though the defense minister announced the operational step.
contrary_evidence: Procurement is an implementation step, not a full command-and-control reform.
The aircraft are for nuclear sharing, not independent German nuclear capability.

evidence.claim: Scholz said Germany would not enter the war directly and rejected a no-fly zone because it would risk direct conflict between NATO and Russia.
evidence.title: Olaf Scholz: "There will be no direct military involvement in the war"
evidence.excerpt: Scholz said Germany would not enter the war directly and rejected a no-fly zone because it would risk direct conflict between NATO and Russia.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct interview transcript with Scholz in a major independent outlet; strong for rhetoric and escalation restraint.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in-period and central to crisis de-escalation choices.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Scholz choice and articulation of escalation boundaries.
contrary_evidence: A no-fly-zone refusal is a restraint choice, but it also reflects alliance limits and caution.
Does not by itself prove broader arms-control leadership.

evidence.claim: Germany, through the NPDI, endorsed transparency, NPT-strengthening, disarmament verification, nuclear risk reduction, and better nuclear safety, security, and safeguards.
evidence.title: Non-Proliferation and Disarmament Initiative - 11th High-level Meeting Joint High-level Statement
evidence.excerpt: Germany, through the NPDI, endorsed transparency, NPT-strengthening, disarmament verification, nuclear risk reduction, and better nuclear safety, security, and safeguards.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary multilateral statement naming Germany as a participant and specifying risk-reduction goals.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and highly relevant to arms-control posture.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the German government under Scholz, though delivered through the NPDI and foreign ministry channels.
contrary_evidence: Multilateral statements can be aspirational and not implementation evidence.
The source does not isolate Scholz's personal role in drafting.

evidence.claim: Scholz and Biden said Moscow's latest nuclear threats were irresponsible and would have exceptionally serious consequences, framing the response as escalation control rather than brinkmanship.
evidence.title: Scholz, Biden agree Kremlin's nuclear threats 'irresponsible' in phonecall
evidence.excerpt: Scholz and Biden said Moscow's latest nuclear threats were irresponsible and would have exceptionally serious consequences, framing the response as escalation control rather than brinkmanship.
evidence.source_locator: lead paragraph and quoted government statement
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report on a contemporaneous Scholz-Biden call; strong evidence for crisis rhetoric and allied coordination.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 during the nuclear-threat phase of the Ukraine war.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Scholz's crisis messaging and alliance coordination.
contrary_evidence: The call is about rhetoric and alliance signaling, not a concrete treaty or force-control decision.
It remains a mediated report rather than a verbatim transcript.

evidence.claim: After visiting Beijing, Scholz said the joint rejection of nuclear weapons use in Ukraine was reason enough for the trip, and the readout said Germany and China jointly opposed the use or threat of nuclear weapons.
evidence.title: Scholz: Xi opposing nuclear weapons in Ukraine reason enough to visit China
evidence.excerpt: After visiting Beijing, Scholz said the joint rejection of nuclear weapons use in Ukraine was reason enough for the trip, and the readout said Germany and China jointly opposed the use or threat of nuclear weapons.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report on a contemporaneous diplomatic statement; strong for risk-reduction rhetoric and external coordination.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and relevant to global nuclear-risk signaling.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Scholz diplomacy, though the substantive statement was joint with Xi and therefore partly shared.
contrary_evidence: A joint statement with China is signaling, not binding arms control.
China's agreement was limited and did not amount to policy convergence on Russia.

unresolved_gaps: No primary record of a Scholz-led command-and-control, custody, or safety reform in 2022.
The strongest direct evidence is signaling and procurement, not measured risk-reduction outcomes.
No private cabinet, NATO, or Russian-channel records showing the full decision chain behind caution, escalation limits, and ceasefire efforts.
No enacted 2022 Scholz-led federal police-oversight, complaint, or anti-racism reform was recovered.
The record is stronger on baseline freedoms, court protection, and limited reforms than on direct Scholz-led 2022 expansion of contestability.
Household-level distribution and long-run productivity effects remain thinner than the policy and macro response record.
Independent 2022 outcome data on take-up, distribution, and durability of the social measures is limited.
No direct, independently verified evidence of personal enrichment, family/business conflict, or nepotism was recovered.
The central Cum-Ex dispute still lacks the original transcript or decision PDF needed to resolve the truthfulness question cleanly.
Direct personnel, delegation, and implementation-discipline evidence is thinner than program, budget, procurement, and outcome evidence.
Some outcome indicators are partly inherited or shock-driven, so causal attribution for 2022 success remains mixed.
